g.text: You tell the story as a C4 model in Kubernetes. The operator scaffolds one Git repository per Container, Crews turn ready issues into Tasks, agents implement and review them in sandboxes, and
only what passes CI and review is merged.
Tell the story first: who uses what, and why.
kubectl, GitOps or the UI: anything can write the model.
CEL rules and an admission policy guard the model; the UI
Each Container gets its own repository, once.

App skeleton, .devcontainer/, AGENTS.md and role guides, CI.
Agents do the work; the platform decides what merges.
Issues with context, goal and acceptance
criteria, in milestones. A milestone with a
due date is a release. Ready issues get
status/* labels say where each issue is;
priority/urgent jumps the queue. Issues can
• No acceptance criteria: back to a person, before any tokens are spent.
• Needs a protected file: the Task waits, the operator carries the change.
• Usage limit or node restart: wait or run again, no round lost.
• Out of rounds and tries: back to a person (status/needs-human).

People and agents work in devcontainers; a
small client registers a Session and sends a
heartbeat every 30 s. Silent for 2 minutes:
Every Task keeps its timeline in status.history.
Quality comes from what the platform enforces.
• No Kubernetes credentials in the sandbox; results leave through the pod's termination
• A Gitea bot user per Container, with write access to its own repository only.
• No pushes to main: only the operator merges, and only the reviewed commit.
• CI, the Makefile, the agents' rules and .theos.yaml change only through a gated
• A NetworkPolicy allows DNS, Gitea and public HTTPS; every run has a deadline.
Where it runs: a Kubernetes cluster
Container, Crew, Task and Session controllers.
Repositories, issues, pull requests and CI.
One pod per agent run, implementer or reviewer.
Reads the API with GET only, plus metrics-server.
Built on it so far: v1 scaffolds Containers from a catalog · v2 agents build the apps · v3 the Factory view · v4 Crews of agents with roles build from issues. Spec: docs/design.md.
